answer: Diminishing spillover cost curve.** Each new identity's registration fee scales with the number of identities already linked to the same funding source or behavioral cluster, rising exponentially rather than linearly. An attacker's marginal cost per additional agent grows steeply past a small horizon of free slots, so mass creation becomes uneconomic. The system infers linkage from shared timing pigment in transaction metadata and shared counterparties. A crystal-clear audit log prices every cluster expansion, forcing attackers to pay superlinear totals for each wave.
